claims.explanation: Bergenin's anti-inflammatory activity via NF-κB/MAPK inhibition and PPARγ agonism likely sensitizes lines with intact inflammatory/NF-κB signaling and antioxidant pathways, while lines with KEAP1/NRF2 or PTEN alterations that constitutively activate survival and antioxidant programs are protected. The selective killing pattern is best explained by loss of STK11/LKB1 or PTEN, which impairs AMPK-mediated metabolic stress responses and increases dependence on NF-κB-driven survival, making these lines hypersensitive to bergenin's combined anti-inflammatory and oxidative-stress-inducing effects.

features.basis: Observed in multiple selectively killed lines (22RV1, SNU840, G361, TE4 is least affected but others); LKB1 loss impairs AMPK stress response
Observed in least-affected lines (BT549, WM793, TE4, U118MG); PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT survival
LUDLU1 (least affected) has KEAP1 mutation; NRF2 activation protects against oxidative stress induced by bergenin
Bergenin inhibits NF-κB signaling; high NF-κB activity may indicate dependence
Bergenin targets TNF and inhibits its production; lines with high TNF signaling may be more affected
Bergenin annotated as IL1B inhibitor; inflammatory signaling dependence may sensitize
Bergenin acts as PPARγ agonist; lines expressing PPARγ may respond
TP53 mutation common in killed lines but also in least affected; weak evidence
BRAF mutations in several killed lines (22RV1, G361, RPMI7951, 8305C, MDAMB361, UACC62) but also in least affected (WM793, K029AX)
Bergenin induces Nrf2 via mTOR/β-TrcP pathway; high NRF2 may protect
Bergenin modulates MAPK signaling; MAPK-dependent lines may be sensitive
Bergenin improves SIRT1 expression; low SIRT1 may sensitize to NF-κB inhibition
